newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices firm this week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices firm this week.

text.p: Australian wool prices strengthened this week with strong demand for the stylish wools on offer at sales in Goulburn, Adelaide and Fremantle, Wesfarmers Dalgety said.
The eastern market indicator rose 11 cents on the week to 564 cents a kg clean, while the western market indicator rose eight cents to 517 cents a kg clean.
Of the 84,411 bales offered, 7.9 percent was passed in.
A bale of 15.4 micron superfine wool sold at 5,600 cents a kg greasy to Italian spinner Loro Paina at Goulburn for a seasonal record in the northern region.

Wesfarmers said there was a 'squeeze' on the market as many buyers recognised prices were attractive enough to profitably cover previously sold positions and were under pressure to meet shipment dates before the end of the month.

"It is questionable whether this upturn can be sustained in the immediate term as there seem to be limited new orders available and the upcoming offering is generally less stylish. "However, grower resistance is likely to prevent prices falling too far beyond current levels," Wesfarmers said.
In the futures market, a total of 284 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended October 17.
